hobbies.title: Autonomous Agent Tinkering
hobbies.narrative: Obsessed with fully autonomous agents. Started with OpenClaw, defected to Hermes, then came crawling back — by forking OpenClaw into my own custom claw. Next on the list: world domination. (Just kidding... unless?)
hobbies.details: My custom claw fork automates recurring life admin end to end — if I catch myself doing something twice, the agent inherits the job. It also controls my home lights, so if they flicker, I know my agent is angry.

experiences.diaryNarrative: As my Tokyo chapter was closing, a stealth map startup asked me to be their first engineer. So I said yes to a blank repo and a mandate: build the whole platform. 220 million map features later, I'm still saying yes to blank repos.
resumeBulletPoints: Joined as the first engineering hire; now lead 3 engineers and own the platform architecture, data-ingestion and CI/CD pipelines, and code review

Designed and shipped the flagship map-tile serving architecture — a hybrid pipeline (pre-emptive regeneration on data change + cache-on-serve) that delivers live-updating tiles at static-tile cost, with the whole stack containerized and run on Docker Compose. Serves 220M+ features (70M building frames, 8K+ indoor sites, 150M+ outdoor POIs); cut worst-case tile latency from >1 min to ~50 ms; load-tested to 200K users

Lead development of a waste-collection logistics platform: route planning, collection-point management, truck scheduling, an iPad driver app, real-time GPS tracking, a self-hosted LiveKit calling server, and an analytics dashboard — in production with 3 commercial sanitation operators, 24/7

Shipped applied-AI systems: a voice LLM concierge for a large Hokkaido commercial complex (GPT-6 Luna + GPT-Live-1 real-time voice; ~150 interactions/day), a natural-language GIS exploration + internal-support agent (locally fine-tuned Qwen-3.5-27B; Unlimited-OCR + vector search over internal docs), and a computer-vision inventory pipeline (SAM + DINO) that lets one operator do the counting work of five

experiences.diaryNarrative: Discovered the magic — and the menace — of PostGIS. Spent too many late nights debugging polygons with holes in all the wrong places. Just four of us at the start, building one basemap for all of Japan. Geometry broke me before I learned to tame it.
resumeBulletPoints: First engineering hire on an in-house indoor/outdoor location platform (team of 4); owned the full mapping stack — basemap, indoor rendering, POI, and wayfinding — built 0→1
Sole hands-on engineer for the first 4 months; built the PoCs and demos that won division funding, then became the largest individual contributor across web, backend, and iOS as the team grew 4→11
Delivered a Japan-wide basemap and ~100 indoor venues; the platform secured 7 paying company contracts
Shipped the platform's first commercial product — employee-location and vehicle build-progress tracking for a major automotive manufacturer (BLE positioning; RFID + QR scanning station-to-station)
Built an LLM-assisted natural-language POI search (embeddings + PGroonga)
Stack: MapLibre GL, Planetiler, OSM + GSI data, PostGIS (routing), Swift/iOS, Azure

experiences.diaryNarrative: Spent two years turning buildings into browsable maps for a heavy-industry giant — and doubling as the English↔Japanese interpreter whenever the overseas partners showed up. Shipped across 15+ sites and learned that "indoor GPS" is a small lie we all agree to tell.
resumeBulletPoints: Built a browser-based indoor mapping platform for a major heavy-industry client (Kawasaki Heavy Industries, via dispatch)
Delivered indoor↔outdoor routing, a map SDK shipped via CDN/NPM, a geofencing system, BLE-beacon configuration tooling, and customer/employee analytics dashboards deployed across 15+ client sites
Served as the English↔Japanese bridge in foreign-partner technical meetings
Stack: React/Next.js, Node.js, Rust (WASM), MSSQL, Cosmos DB, Azure DevOps

experiences.diaryNarrative: On day one as an intern, they handed me real vessel data. I spent 40% of the time building dashboards and 60% perfecting my "deeply focused" face whenever the boss walked by. The failure-prediction model I trained is somehow still running in production in 2026.
resumeBulletPoints: Built a d3.js analytics dashboard that replaced a manual Excel reporting workflow, and a part-failure prediction model (~70% accuracy) adopted for pre-emptive vessel checks — still in production in 2026
